characters.name: Frodo Baggins
clues: Both of this character's parents died in a boating accident long before any adventure began.
A beloved older relative adopted this character, then left behind his home and a small golden trinket.
A wound from a cursed blade, taken beneath a ruined watchtower on a hill, still ached a year later.
At a council in Rivendell, this character volunteered to carry a dangerous object to the land where it was made.
At the Cracks of Doom this character could not give up the Ring willingly, and lost a finger to the creature who seized it.

references.supports: Parents died in a boating accident; adopted by Bilbo; Morgul-knife wound on Weathertop; volunteered at the Council of Elrond; finger bitten off by Gollum at Mount Doom.
One year after the stabbing the wound in Frodo's shoulder ached again.
Weathertop is a hill with the ruins of a tower.

characters.name: Samwise Gamgee
clues: Raised by a gardener, this character loved plants, tales of the Elves and a quiet life.
Caught eavesdropping beneath a window, this character was sent on a journey instead of being punished.
A small box of soil from an elven lady's orchard later brought trees back to a ravaged homeland.
When a giant spider seemed to have killed his master, this character took up the burden himself for a time.
This character carried his master up the slopes of Mount Doom when strength failed, and later served many terms as Mayor of the Shire.

references.supports: Gardener's son; overheard by Gandalf under the window; Galadriel's gift of earth from her orchard; took the Ring in Cirith Ungol; carried Frodo up Mount Doom; Mayor of the Shire.

characters.name: Gandalf
clues: One of a handful of beings who came from across the Sea in the guise of an old man, sent to advise and persuade the free peoples.
A wanderer with a fondness for fireworks, rarely seen without his pipe.
This character fell in battle with a fire-demon on a bridge in the deep dark, and returned in a brighter form.
This character bore a ring of fire, given long before by the shipwright of the Grey Havens.
Clad in grey, then in white after returning from death, this wizard rode Shadowfax, lord of horses.

references.supports: One of the Istari; fireworks; usually seen with a pipe; fall on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm and return as Gandalf the White; Narya passed to him by Círdan; rode Shadowfax.
The mission of the Istari was to advise and persuade Men and Elves to resist Sauron.

characters.name: Aragorn
clues: Raised in secret by an elf-lord, this character was long hidden under a different name.
Heir to a line of kings that traced its descent from Elendil, though no king had ruled that line's realm for ages.
A Ranger of the North, this character guided four small travelers through the wild lands of Eriador.
This character looked into a seeing-stone and openly challenged the Dark Lord.
Crowned king of both Gondor and Arnor, this character wed the daughter of Elrond.

references.supports: Fostered in Rivendell under another name; descent from Elendil; Ranger who guided the hobbits from Bree; used the Orthanc-stone to show himself to Sauron; crowned King of the Reunited Kingdom; married Arwen.
Strider offers guidance and protection to the hobbits at Bree.
Strider leads the hobbits out of Bree toward Weathertop.

characters.name: Legolas
clues: The son of a king, this character was sent from a northern forest realm to carry news to Rivendell.
Light of foot, this character could walk on top of snow without sinking, on a mountain pass in winter.
This character and a Dwarf became fast friends, though their peoples had long been at odds.
At the cries of seabirds, this character first felt the call of the Sea that no Elf can long resist.
The only Elf among the nine travelers, this archer shot down the winged steed of a Ringwraith over the Great River.

references.supports: Son of Thranduil; messenger to Rivendell; walked on snow on Caradhras; friendship with Gimli; heard gulls at Pelargir; shot the Nazgûl's steed over the Anduin.

characters.name: Gimli
clues: This character's father had been one of the company that once set out to reclaim a mountain from a dragon.
This character asked an elven lady for a single strand of her hair and was given three.
Alongside a Ranger and an Elf, this character ran for many days in pursuit of a band of Orcs.
At a great fortress in a mountain valley, this character fought on the wall, and afterwards marveled at the glittering caves behind it.
Many years after the War of the Ring, this character sailed West in the company of an Elf who had become his closest friend.

references.supports: Son of Glóin of Thorin's company; three strands of Galadriel's hair; pursuit across Rohan; Helm's Deep and the Glittering Caves; fought beside Legolas; sailed West (Fo.A. 120).
Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli pursue the captured hobbits for many days.

characters.name: Gollum
clues: This character's life was ruined by the murder of a friend over a gleaming find in a riverbed.
Exiled from his own kin, this character lived for centuries in the dark beneath a mountain range, eating raw fish.
A riddle contest with a stranger in the dark ended with the loss of the only thing this character cared for.
This character guided two travelers toward a mountain of fire, torn between a sworn oath and a terrible craving.
At the Cracks of Doom this character bit off a finger to take the Ring, then toppled into the fire with it.

references.supports: Murdered Déagol over the Ring; exiled and lived under the Misty Mountains; riddle game with Bilbo; guided Frodo and Sam to Mordor; bit off Frodo's finger and fell into the fire.

characters.name: Sauron
clues: Before turning to evil, this being served a smith among the Powers and loved order and craft.
Posing as a fair emissary, this being taught the Elven-smiths of a western land to make rings.
This being allowed himself to be carried captive to a great island, then corrupted its king until the island was swallowed by the sea.
At the end of the Second Age, a prince cut a ring from this being's hand with the broken blade of his father's sword.
Ruler of Mordor from the Dark Tower, served by nine Ringwraiths and symbolized by a lidless eye.

references.supports: Maia of Aulë; fair guise and the Rings of Power; captivity in Númenor and its Downfall; Isildur cut the Ring from his hand; Barad-dûr, Nazgûl, the Eye.
Isildur used Narsil's broken blade to cut the Ring from Sauron's hand.
The Eye is also called the Lidless Eye.

characters.name: Galadriel
clues: Born in the Blessed Realm, this character had seen a light that no longer shines.
This character ruled a realm of golden-leaved trees alongside her husband.
This character kept a basin of water that showed things that were, things that are, and things that yet may be.
A small traveler offered this character the Ring of Power, and she pictured herself as a terrible queen before refusing it.
Bearer of Nenya, the ring of adamant, this character gave the Fellowship cloaks, gifts, and a phial holding the light of a star.

references.supports: Born in Aman and saw the Two Trees; ruled Lothlórien with Celeborn; Mirror of Galadriel; refused the Ring; bearer of Nenya; gifts to the Fellowship including the Phial.
Lothlórien described as a golden wood with mallorn trees.

characters.name: Boromir
clues: The elder of two sons of a Steward, this character was admired by many and the pride of his father.
This character carried a great horn, tipped with silver, and sounded it in a time of need.
A recurring dream that troubled his family sent this character north through hard country to a council in Rivendell.
At a council this character argued that the Ring should be used as a weapon in the defense of his city.
This character died at Amon Hen defending two hobbits from Orcs, after he had tried to take the Ring by force.

references.supports: Elder son of Denethor; great horn tipped with silver, sounded in Moria; dream and journey to Rivendell; argued at the Council of Elrond; died defending Merry and Pippin at Amon Hen after trying to seize the Ring.

characters.name: Bilbo Baggins
clues: This character was a respectable, comfort-loving soul until an unexpected party of guests changed everything.
This character was hired as a burglar by a company seeking to reclaim a mountain and its treasure.
In a dark cave, this character found a magic ring, then won a game of riddles against the creature who had lost it.
This character wrote the story of his journey, which later became part of the Red Book of Westmarch.
After vanishing from his own eleventy-first birthday party, this character eventually left Middle-earth over the Sea.

references.supports: Hired as burglar by Thorin's company; found the Ring and won the riddle game; authored the Red Book material; vanished at his 111th birthday; sailed West.

characters.name: Saruman
clues: Head of an order sent from across the Sea, this character was a deep student of the lore of the Rings.
This character made his home in a black tower inside a ringed fortress, where he kept a seeing-stone.
Gazing into a stone of far-seeing, this character was ensnared by his greater enemy and betrayed his task.
This character's fires felled forests, and in pits beneath his tower he bred a stronger kind of Orc.
After his fall, this character took over the Shire under an assumed name, and was finally killed by his own former servant.

references.supports: Head of the Istari; Orthanc and its palantír; corruption through the palantír; felling of trees and Uruk-hai; occupation of the Shire as "Sharkey" and death at Gríma's hand.

characters.name: Faramir
clues: The younger of two brothers, this character was a lover of lore and music who was overlooked by his father.
This character captained a company of Rangers who ambushed enemy soldiers in a green land west of Mordor.
In a hidden refuge behind a waterfall, this character questioned two hobbits and, though tempted by their burden, let them go.
After a doomed sortie ordered by his father, this character lay near death, struck down by the Black Breath.
Healed in the Houses of Healing, this character fell in love with a shieldmaiden of Rohan, and was later raised to a princely title in the land he had defended.

references.supports: Younger son of Denethor, lover of lore; Captain of the Rangers of Ithilien; Henneth Annûn and Frodo; Black Breath after Osgiliath; married Éowyn and became Prince of Ithilien.

characters.name: Éowyn
clues: This character's greatest fear was not death but being left behind in a life of dull duty.
This character's brother was imprisoned for disobedience on the orders of a sly advisor.
In disguise, this character rode into war with a small hobbit on her saddle.
This character confronted the Lord of the Nazgûl and declared herself no man, fulfilling an old prophecy.
This character's longing for war faded, and she married a prince of Ithilien.

references.supports: Fear of a cage; rode as Dernhelm with Merry; slew the Witch-king; met Faramir in the Houses of Healing and married him.
On Gríma's orders Éomer was arrested and imprisoned for his disobedience.
Éowyn's longing for war faded and she agreed to wed Faramir.

characters.name: Théoden
clues: This ruler aged before his time under the whispered influence of a servant who served another master.
A wizard freed this ruler from a weakened state, and he stood tall again.
This ruler's only son and heir fell in battle against a wizard's forces at a river crossing.
This ruler retreated to a fortress in a mountain valley, where his people won a battle that earned him a new name meaning the Renewed.
This ruler died on the Pelennor Fields, crushed by his fallen horse, after leading a great charge at dawn.

references.supports: Under Gríma's influence; healed by Gandalf; Théodred fell at the Fords of Isen; retreated to Helm's Deep, won the Battle of the Hornburg and became known as Ednew, the Renewed; death on the Pelennor Fields beneath Snowmane.

characters.name: Elrond
clues: This character's twin brother chose a mortal life, and he chose to remain among the Elves.
As a child, this character was taken captive in the sack of his parents' haven, yet came to love one of his captors, a son of an ancient smith.
This character served as herald to the High King in a great war at the end of the Second Age.
This character healed a hobbit of a wound from a cursed blade and presided over a council deciding the fate of the Ring.
Master of a hidden valley, bearer of the ring of sapphire, this character was the father of Arwen.

references.supports: Twin Elros chose mortality; taken captive at the sack of the Havens and came to love Maglor; herald of Gil-galad; healed Frodo; Council of Elrond; bearer of Vilya; father of Arwen.

characters.name: Treebeard
clues: This character and his kin learned to speak from the Elves, in a time when the world was young.
A shepherd of trees who never says anything in haste, this character had long lost his wife.
This character took two hobbits as guests and gave them a draught that made them grow taller.
This character called a great assembly of his people that lasted for days.
This character led his people to break a dam and flood the stronghold of a wizard.

references.supports: Ents taught to speak by the Elves; the lost Entwives; Ent-draughts and Merry and Pippin's growth; the Entmoot; the flooding of Isengard.
The Ent-draughts taken by Merry and Pippin added three inches or more to their heights.
The Entmoot lasted for days before the Ents resolved to attack Isengard.
The attackers broke the dam, which flooded Isengard.

characters.name: Tom Bombadil
clues: This cheerful character wears a blue coat and yellow boots, and answers most questions in song.
This character's wife is known as the River-daughter.
This character freed travelers from a malevolent willow and from a wight in a burial mound.
This character claims to have known the first raindrop and the first acorn.
This character put on the Ring without turning invisible, and it seemed to have no hold on him.

references.supports: Blue coat and yellow boots; Goldberry, called the River-daughter; rescue from Old Man Willow and the barrow-wight; the oldest, remembering the first raindrop and acorn; unaffected by the Ring.
Goldberry is called the River-daughter; her parentage is uncertain on the page.

characters.name: Gríma Wormtongue
clues: This character was a royal advisor whose silken words were more poison than counsel.
This character lusted after his king's niece, and hoped to win her as the price of his treachery.
This character secretly served a wizard while holding a place of trust at a royal court.
From a high window, this character hurled a heavy dark globe at those standing below, nearly striking one of them.
In the end this character killed his former master on a doorstep in the Shire and was shot dead by hobbit archers.

references.supports: Royal advisor to Théoden; desire for Éowyn; agent of Saruman; threw the palantír from Orthanc; killed Saruman at Bag End and was shot by hobbits.

characters.name: Denethor
clues: This character was never a king, yet in all but name he ruled his realm for decades.
This character studied a seeing-stone in secret, until he saw only the hopeless things the Enemy chose to show.
This character loved his elder son and neglected the younger, who loved him dearly.
On receiving the shards of a broken horn, this character mourned his firstborn and began to sink into despair.
Driven mad by despair, this character tried to burn himself and his gravely wounded son on a pyre.

references.supports: Ruling Steward of Gondor; use of the Anor palantír and despair; preference for Boromir over Faramir; the broken Horn of Gondor; the pyre.

characters.name: Thorin Oakenshield
clues: Heir to a kingdom lost to a dragon, this character worked a humble trade in exile.
One of thirteen Dwarves, this character led them, a wizard and a burglar on a long journey east.
A wizard gave this character a map and a key at the start of the quest.
Dragon-sickness took hold of this character inside the mountain, and he would not share the treasure.
Mortally wounded at the Battle of Five Armies, this character apologized to the burglar for his harsh words before he died.

references.supports: Exile in the Blue Mountains; led the company of thirteen; map and key from Gandalf; dragon-sickness; wounded at the Battle of Five Armies and apologized to Bilbo on his deathbed.

characters.name: Smaug
clues: Drawn by the wealth of a Dwarf kingdom, this creature drove its people into exile.
Asleep upon a hoard of treasure, this creature noticed that a single cup was missing and flew into a rage.
This creature's underside was crusted with gems, except for one bare patch that a thrush reported to an archer.
This creature burned a town built on a lake before it was slain.
A single black arrow, shot by an archer of Lake-town, killed this creature in the end.

references.supports: Attack on Erebor; theft of a cup; the bare patch on the underbelly and the thrush; destruction of Lake-town; slain by Bard with the Black Arrow.

characters.name: Beorn
clues: This character keeps bees and tame horses in a wooden hall, and speaks to animals.
This character is a man who can take the shape of a great black bear.
After suspicious questioning, this character sheltered a company of Dwarves for several days and lent them ponies.
This character arrived at a great battle just in time, in the shape of an enormous bear.
After the battle this character became a great chief and founded a line whose members were said to take bear-shape in times of need.

references.supports: Keeper of bees and tame horses; changes between man and bear; hosted the Dwarves and lent ponies; fought at the Battle of Five Armies; became a great chief with bear-shifting descendants.
Beorn keeps bees and tame horses in his wooden hall.

characters.name: Peregrin Took
clues: The youngest of a band of cousins, this character often spoke before thinking.
This character looked into a seeing-stone and was forced to face the Dark Lord's gaze.
This character pledged allegiance to the grieving Steward of Gondor and became a guard of his citadel.
At the Black Gate this character slew a troll, and was found crushed beneath its body.
Late in life this character became Thain of the Shire, and was later laid to rest in Gondor beside an old friend.

references.supports: Youngest of the four hobbits; looked in the Orthanc-stone; pledged allegiance to Denethor and became a Guard of the Citadel; killed a troll at the Black Gate; became Thain; buried in Rath Dínen.

characters.name: Fëanor
clues: This character's mother grew weary of life after his birth, and chose not to return to it.
This character crafted three jewels that held the light of the Two Trees.
With his seven sons, this character swore an oath that bound his house for ages.
This character burned the ships at Losgar, leaving part of his people behind on the far shore.
This character was mortally wounded by balrogs during the Battle-under-Stars, and his body burned to ash.

references.supports: Míriel's fading after his birth; the Silmarils; the Oath with his seven sons; burning of the ships at Losgar; death by Gothmog and balrogs in Dagor-nuin-Giliath.

characters.name: Fingolfin
clues: Half-brother of a rebellious smith, this character led the larger part of a host across a sea of ice.
After being left behind, this character crossed the frozen straits at the top of the world.
This character rode alone to a dark fortress and challenged its master to single combat.
This character wounded his foe seven times, and some of those wounds never fully healed.
This character fell to the Dark Lord after the duel, and the king of the Eagles carried his body to a mountaintop.

references.supports: Half-brother of Fëanor; crossing of the Helcaraxë; challenged Morgoth to single combat at Angband; wounded him seven times, his wounds never fully healing; body rescued by Thorondor and brought to a mountaintop.

characters.name: Túrin Turambar
clues: Sent away as a child by his mother, this character was fostered in an Elven kingdom.
A curse on this character's family was spoken by the Dark Lord himself, because of his father's defiance.
This character wielded a black sword that spoke at the last.
This character slew a dragon by striking it from below, but its dying words revealed a dreadful truth about his wife.
This character ended his own life by falling upon his sword after losing his family.

references.supports: Fostered in Doriath; Morgoth's curse on Húrin's kin; Gurthang; slaying of Glaurung and revelation about Níniel; death on his sword at Cabed-en-Aras.
Húrin refused Morgoth, and the Dark Lord cursed his kin.
The black sword answers Túrin in a cold voice before his death.
Glaurung's last words reveal Níniel's identity; Túrin then casts himself upon his sword.
Túrin found Glaurung over the gorge of Cabed-en-Aras and approached from below.

characters.name: Eärendil
clues: Born in a hidden city, this character saw it fall as a child.
A ship built at the Havens by Elven shipwrights carried this character in search of the West.
This character's wife was the granddaughter of a famed mortal and an elven princess.
This character sailed into the uncharted West and pleaded there on behalf of Elves and Men.
Set in the heavens with a holy jewel on his brow, this character became a star seen at dusk and at dawn.

references.supports: Born in Gondolin and left to escape its fall; Vingilot built with Círdan; married Elwing, granddaughter of Beren and Lúthien; embassy to Valinor; set in the sky bearing a Silmaril.

characters.name: Beren
clues: A mortal outlaw, this character saw his father and his companions fall to a dark lord's hunters.
A ring given to this character's father by an elven king, in thanks for saving his life, became a family heirloom.
This character won the heart of an immortal maiden, and her father demanded a seemingly impossible price.
The price was a jewel from the Dark Lord's crown, and this character lost his hand to a great wolf.
After falling to the wolf, this character was allowed to return to life, and lived out his years with his wife.

references.supports: Barahir's band slain; Finrod's ring; Thingol's bride-price; the Silmaril and Carcharoth taking his hand; return from Mandos.
Finrod gave Barahir his ring after Barahir saved his life; Beren's quest repaid that debt.

characters.name: Lúthien
clues: A king's daughter, this character was also the child of a being of divine race.
Her beauty was said to be the fairest that ever was among the children of the world.
With her magic and her dance, this character put a Dark Lord into a deep sleep.
This character was imprisoned by her own father in a house built among the branches of a great beech, and escaped by her magic.
This character chose to die like Men in order to share the fate of her husband.

references.supports: Daughter of Thingol and Melian; her beauty; put Morgoth to sleep with her magic and dance; escape from Hírilorn; chose mortality with Beren.
Thingol imprisoned Lúthien in a house among the branches of Hírilorn; she escaped using her magical arts.

characters.name: Finrod Felagund
clues: This character was the first of his people to meet Men, and he valued their friendship.
This character founded a vast underground fortress and ruled it for many years.
This character gave a ring as a pledge of friendship to a mortal who had saved his life.
This character matched songs against a dark lord's servant in a duel of power at a tower.
This character died in a dungeon at the hands of a werewolf, slain while saving a mortal companion.

references.supports: First Elf to meet Men; founded Nargothrond; ring given to Barahir; singing contest against Sauron; death in Tol-in-Gaurhoth fighting a werewolf to save Beren.

characters.name: Thingol
clues: This character stood spellbound in a woodland for years, and awoke as ruler of an Elven people.
This character's realm was ringed by a girdle of enchantment, woven by his wife, that kept out unwelcome visitors.
This character set an impossible bride-price: a jewel from the crown of the Dark Lord.
Greed for a jewel set in a necklace led a party of Dwarves to murder this character.
After this character's death his wife left, the girdle fell, and his kingdom was ruined.

references.supports: Enchanted by Melian in Nan Elmoth; the Girdle of Melian; demanded a Silmaril of Beren; slain by Dwarves over the Nauglamír; Melian's departure and the ruin of Doriath.
Melian set the Girdle around Doriath; on Thingol's death she departed and the Girdle vanished.

characters.name: Círdan
clues: This character was among the oldest Elves still dwelling in Middle-earth at the end of the Third Age.
A master of ships, this character ruled a haven on the western coast.
This character gave a ring of fire to a newly arrived wizard.
This character helped build the ship in which a famous mariner sailed in search of the West.
This character prepared the last ship that bore the Ring-bearers over the Sea.

references.supports: Teleri Elf who stayed in Middle-earth; lord of the Grey Havens; gave Narya to Gandalf; helped with Eärendil's ship; the last ship carrying Frodo, Bilbo and Gandalf.

characters.name: Celebrimbor
clues: Grandson of the greatest of the Elven craftsmen, this character did not follow his father in his oath.
This character led the guild of Elven-smiths in a western realm called Hollin.
This character alone forged three rings that were kept free of the enemy's touch.
This character hid the three rings before his realm fell, and was tortured for their whereabouts.
After his death this character's body was displayed as a banner by the host that destroyed his realm.

references.supports: Grandson of Fëanor, stayed in Nargothrond against his father's oath; leader of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain; forged the Three; hid them; tortured and killed by Sauron; body used as a banner.

characters.name: Ungoliant
clues: The origins of this creature are a mystery, though some of the Elves suspected a spirit corrupted by the Dark Lord at the beginning of time.
This creature devoured light and spun darkness in its place.
This creature drained the Two Trees of their light until they withered.
This creature demanded the jewels the Dark Lord had stolen, and he refused her.
This creature's end is uncertain, but it is said she devoured herself in her hunger.

references.supports: Origins shrouded in mystery, thought by some Eldar to be an Ainu corrupted by Melkor; devoured light and spun Unlight; destroyed the Two Trees; Melkor refused her the jewels; said by some to have devoured herself.

characters.name: Elendil
clues: This character escaped the drowning of a great island with a fleet of ships.
This character led those of his people who had stayed faithful to the Valar.
This character founded two kingdoms in exile and was High King over both, ruling from the north.
This character fell in battle against the Dark Lord at the end of the Second Age, and his sword was broken beneath him.
This character's broken sword gave a shard that his son used to cut the Ring from the enemy's hand.

references.supports: Escaped the Downfall of Númenor; leader of the Faithful; High King of Arnor and Gondor (with Isildur and Anárion); death at the hand of Sauron and the shattering of Narsil; Isildur's use of the shard.

characters.name: Meriadoc Brandybuck
clues: As a teenager, this character watched a hobbit turn invisible to avoid a meeting, then looked into that hobbit's private diary.
At the gate of a Dwarf-city, a wizard commended this character as being on the right track with the riddle, though it was accidental.
Held captive once by a willow tree and once by a barrow-wight, this character was rescued both times by the same rescuer, who let the hobbits keep the daggers found in the barrow.
This character offered a king of Rohan his service, was told to stay behind, and rode to war secretly behind a young rider.
On the Pelennor Fields this character stabbed the sinew behind the knee of the leader of the Nazgûl with a blade from a burial mound, breaking the spell that protected him.

references.supports: Saw Bilbo become invisible to avoid a meeting and looked into his private diary; Gandalf commended him at the gate of Moria for being on the right track with the riddle; captured by Old Man Willow and by a Barrow-wight and rescued by Tom Bombadil, who told the hobbits to keep the Barrow daggers; offered his service to Théoden, was forbidden to ride to war and rode with Dernhelm; pierced the sinew behind the Witch-king's knee with the Barrow-blade.
The Witch-king is the chief of the Nazgûl; Merry's wound to his leg and Éowyn's killing blow on the Pelennor Fields.

characters.name: Arwen
clues: This character inherited an elven jewel that had passed from her grandmother to her mother.
Her father ruled that the man she loved could not marry her until he was king of both Gondor and Arnor.
She wove a black standard worked with mithril, gems and gold, which her brothers carried to her betrothed.
Said to resemble a heroine of the First Age, she, like that heroine, gave up elven immortality to marry a mortal.
This daughter of an Elf-lord wed a king on Mid-year's Day, and passed her own place on the ship West to the Ring-bearer.

references.supports: The Elfstone passed from Galadriel to Celebrían to Arwen; Elrond's condition that Aragorn be king of Gondor and Arnor before they wed; Arwen wove the standard carried by her brothers to Aragorn; resembles Lúthien and, like her, gave up Elven immortality to marry a mortal; wed on Mid-year's Day and gave Frodo passage in her place.

characters.name: Shelob
clues: This creature was the last child of a great spider-like being that mated with and devoured others of her kind in a mountain valley.
Her lair in a mountain range was established long before the Dark Lord raised his tower nearby, and she served no master but herself.
A creature searching for his lost treasure once bowed before her and promised to bring her food.
The Dark Lord let her stay because she was an excellent guard of a pass into his land.
This creature stung a hobbit into a death-like coma, then impaled herself on his friend's sword and was blinded by the light of a phial.

references.supports: Last child of Ungoliant, who mated with and devoured other spider-like creatures in Nan Dungortheb; lair in the Ephel Dúath long before Barad-dûr; served no one but herself; Gollum bowed to her and promised food; Sauron let her stay as a guard of Cirith Ungol; stung Frodo into a death-like coma, impaled herself on Sting and was blinded by the Phial.

characters.name: Bard the Bowman
clues: This heir of the last lord of a ruined city, whose family had fled downriver, lived in a town built on a lake.
He kept an inherited arrow that had never failed him and that he always recovered, saving it for his last shot.
A thrush that had overheard a burglar describe a dragon told him where it had no armor.
After the town burned, he led its people to demand part of the treasure from the Dwarves, and later took a hobbit's share of gold and silver in return for a gem.
Slayer of the dragon that burned his town, he became the first king of rebuilt Dale.

references.supports: Heir of Girion, last Lord of Dale, whose family fled down the River Running; lived in Lake-town; the black arrow he always recovered; the thrush told him of the bare spot; demanded part of the treasure and took Bilbo's fourteenth share for the Arkenstone; slew Smaug and became the first King of restored Dale. (Bard the Bowman redirects to Bard.)

characters.name: Witch-king of Angmar
clues: Around the year 1300 of the Third Age, this being founded a northern realm and exploited the disunity of the three kingdoms that had split from a greater one.
In 1409 his forces besieged and destroyed a famed tower of the Dúnedain; a ruler of Arthedain was slain in the same attack.
An elf-lord foretold that this being would never fall by the hand of man.
In the year 2002 he captured Minas Ithil, a stronghold of Gondor, and in 3019 he led an army from it against Minas Tirith.
Chief of the Nine, he stabbed a hobbit at Weathertop with a blade whose tip broke off in the wound, and he perished on the Pelennor Fields at the hands of a woman and a hobbit.

references.supports: Founded Angmar c. T.A. 1300 and exploited the disunity of Arnor's three successor kingdoms; the siege and destruction of Amon Sûl in 1409 and the death of King Arveleg I; Glorfindel's prophecy that he would not fall by the hand of man; took Minas Ithil and led his army from there in 3019; stabbed Frodo on Weathertop with a Morgul-knife whose tip broke off; slain by Éowyn and Merry. (Requested URL /wiki/Witch-king_of_Angmar redirects here.)

characters.name: Balin
clues: Born in 2763, this Dwarf was only seven years old when a dragon drove his people from their mountain home.
In 2841 he set out with his younger brother and an exiled king toward the Lonely Mountain, but the journey ended when the king was captured.
As his company's look-out, he failed to notice a burglar creeping past him, and later grew fondest of that burglar.
Speaking for his company before a woodland king, his surly answers led to all the Dwarves being imprisoned.
In 2989 he led a colony into an ancient Dwarf-mansion, proclaimed himself its ruler, and was slain by an orc archer at a mere; a later company found his tomb.

references.supports: Born T.A. 2763, seven years old when Smaug took Erebor; went with Thráin II and his brother Dwalin in 2841; the company's look-out and Bilbo's fondest companion; spokesman before the Elvenking whose surly answers led to their confinement; led the Moria expedition of 2989, proclaimed himself Lord of Moria and was killed by an orc archer at Mirrormere; his tomb was found by the Fellowship.

characters.name: Radagast
clues: This being was sent as a guardian to the first Elves at their awakening, though it is unclear what shape he took there or how long he stayed.
In 2851 he aided another wizard's search for the Ring with birds and beasts as spies, acting in good faith and unaware of that wizard's real ambitions.
He lived at the western edge of a great forest, and a fellow wizard scorned him as 'the Simple' and 'the Fool'.
In 3018 he was sent to find a fellow wizard, warned him that the Nazgûl were abroad, and passed on an invitation that unwittingly led to that wizard's capture.
Dressed in earthen brown, he sent a great eagle to a captive wizard on the pinnacle of Orthanc.

references.supports: Guardian sent to Cuiviénen (shape and duration unclear); sent as a Wizard in the form of an old man; dwelt at Rhosgobel; scorned by Saruman as the Simple and the Fool; in T.A. 2851 aided Saruman's Ring search with birds and beasts in good faith; in 3018 sent to find Gandalf, warned him of the Nazgûl and passed on Saruman's invitation, which unwittingly led to Gandalf's capture; wore earthen brown.
Radagast, as Gandalf instructed, sent Gwaihir to Isengard to rescue Gandalf from the pinnacle of Orthanc.

characters.name: Durin's Bane
clues: This being survived the war that ended the First Age by hiding at the roots of a mountain range, where it lay dormant for thousands of years.
In 1980 of the Third Age, miners digging for mithril woke it, and it slew their king.
For about five hundred years it held the halls of a Dwarf-kingdom, and orcs and trolls feared it.
It confronted a company on a narrow bridge, wielding a sword of fire and a many-thonged whip.
It fell when a wizard broke the bridge, but its whip dragged him down too; they fought for days on a mountain peak until it was cast down.

references.supports: Survived the War of Wrath and hid beneath the Misty Mountains for over five millennia; woken by mithril-miners in T.A. 1980, slew Durin VI; Moria was left to the Balrog for about 500 years and Orcs and Trolls feared it; the sword of fire and many-thonged whip on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm; fell when Gandalf broke the bridge, was pursued to the peak of Zirakzigil and cast down.

characters.name: Éomer
clues: At eleven this character lost his father to orc raiders and soon his mother, and was adopted by his uncle, a king.
As Third Marshal he commanded the East-mark from his home in a town of the Folde, and fell into the king's disfavor because of the king's advisor.
He disobeyed a ban on pursuing the orcs who had captured two hobbits, and killed their leader near the edge of a great forest.
Meeting three strangers on the plains, he let them go against his realm's law and lent them horses, asking that they be returned.
Hailed as King of the Mark by his dying uncle, he charged in cold fury at the sight of his fallen sister.

references.supports: Father killed by Orcs when he was eleven and mother died soon after; adopted by Théoden; Third Marshal commanding the East-mark from Aldburg in the Folde; Gríma's influence put him in disfavour; disobeyed the ban to pursue the Orcs that held two hobbits and killed their leader Uglúk near Fangorn; lent horses to Aragorn's party against Rohan's law; hailed King of the Mark by the dying Théoden and charged on seeing Éowyn fallen.

characters.name: Glorfindel
clues: This elf-lord died in a fall with a demon of fire, but the Valar allowed him to be re-embodied in recognition of his deeds and sent him back to Middle-earth.
In 1975 he came with a force from the hidden valley to a northern battle, and foretold that the enemy chief would not fall by the hand of man.
He was chosen to seek the Ring-bearer partly because the Ringwraiths did not frighten him; five of them fled from him.
He set a wounded hobbit on his white horse, which carried the hobbit across a ford.
An elf of Rivendell, tall and golden-haired, he suggested at a great council that the Ring would be safe in the depths of the Sea, but a wizard objected.

references.supports: Fell with a Balrog in the abyss and was re-embodied by Manwë's permission because of his deeds, then sent to Middle-earth; led a force from Rivendell to the Battle of Fornost (T.A. 1975) and prophesied the Witch-king would not fall by the hand of man; chosen to seek the Ring-bearer partly because he did not fear the Ringwraiths (five fled from him); put Frodo on Asfaloth, which carried him over the Ford of Bruinen; at the Council of Elrond first suggested the Ring would be safe in the depths of the Sea, which Gandalf objected to; tall, golden-haired.

characters.name: Thranduil
clues: In autumn this ruler wore a crown of berries and red leaves, and in spring one of woodland flowers.
In the Last Alliance his father fell charging ahead of the signal, and two-thirds of his people perished.
When a shadow fell on the southern part of his forest, he moved north and delved his halls underground, said to be partly in memory of a lost elven city.
He imprisoned a company of Dwarves after they disturbed his feast, but a burglar with a magic ring helped them escape.
Father of an Elf chosen for the Fellowship of the Ring, he besieged a mountain together with the Men of a lake-town.

references.supports: Wore a crown of berries and red leaves in autumn and woodland flowers in spring; Oropher fell at Dagorlad charging before Gil-galad's signal and two-thirds of Thranduil's people died; moved his halls north and underground, partly in memory (it was said) of Menegroth; imprisoned the Dwarves after repeated disturbance of his feast and Bilbo helped them escape; father of Legolas, chosen for the Fellowship; besieged the Mountain with Bard.

characters.name: Haldir
clues: Unlike his two brothers, this elf had travelled beyond his homeland and spoke the Common Speech.
He guarded the northern borders of his forest realm as a marchwarden.
On 15-16 January of 3019, he and his brothers met the Fellowship of the Ring as it arrived in his land.
Because of the old ill-feeling between Elves and Dwarves, he made one of the travelers go blindfolded until his lady said otherwise.
He guided the travelers to Caras Galadhon, and later led them to the boats for their departure.

references.supports: Unlike his brothers Rumil and Orophin he had travelled outside Lórien and knew Westron; a marchwarden guarding the forest's northern borders; he and his brothers met the Fellowship on 15-16 January T.A. 3019; made Gimli go blindfolded until Galadriel said otherwise; guided the Fellowship to Caras Galadhon and later led them to the Elven boats. (Haldir_of_Lorien redirects to Haldir.)

characters.name: Isildur
clues: In disguise, he stole a fruit from a doomed tree in a royal city, and is said to have been grievously wounded by the guards.
When his island homeland sank, he escaped in one of three ships under his command, carrying a young tree.
He ruled a southern kingdom jointly with his brother, their thrones side by side, and lived in a city where he planted a white tree.
He used a shard of his father's broken sword to cut the Ring from the Dark Lord's hand, then ignored the advice of Elf-lords and kept it as payment for his lost kin.
Ambushed by orcs at the Gladden Fields, he put on the Ring to vanish, swam the river, and was shot in the reeds when it slipped from his finger.

references.supports: Stole a fruit of Nimloth in disguise and was reportedly wounded by the King's guards; three of the nine ships of the Downfall were his and the young White Tree sailed in his ship; ruled Gondor jointly with Anárion, lived at Minas Ithil and planted the White Tree there; cut the Ring from Sauron with the hilt-shard of Narsil and ignored the advice of Elrond and Círdan; killed at the Gladden Fields after the Ring slipped from his finger.

characters.name: Gwaihir
clues: He is the brother of another great eagle, and the mightiest of the descendants of Thorondor, the eagle he served in the First Age.
At the time of the War of the Ring, he was the swiftest of the Great Eagles.
He rescued a wizard from the pinnacle of a tower on an autumn night, but could not carry him far and left him at a city of horse-lords.
Sent by a lady, he found the wizard on a high peak after a great fight and carried him to Lothlórien.
After the Ring's destruction, he and two other eagles flew into Mordor and carried two hobbits out.

references.supports: Mightiest of the descendants of Thorondor and brother of Landroval; swiftest of the Great Eagles at the time of the War of the Ring; rescued Gandalf from the pinnacle of Orthanc and left him at Edoras; sent by Galadriel to find Gandalf on Celebdil and carried him to Lothlórien; with Landroval and Meneldor carried Frodo and Sam out of Mordor. The page marks the identification with the Eagle of The Hobbit as disputed; no clue uses it.

characters.name: Dáin Ironfoot
clues: At thirty-two, this Dwarf beheaded an orc chieftain with a red axe before the East-gate of a great Dwarf-hall.
Looking alone past that gate, he judged that his people could not return to the hall at that time, and dissuaded a king from entering it.
For more than a century he ruled a land of hills in the north, making his people the strongest in Wilderland.
He marched to a great battle with over five hundred Dwarves, meaning to drive off Elves and Men until a wizard warned him of orcs.
After the previous king fell, he became King under the Mountain, and died aged over 250 defending the body of a king of Dale.

references.supports: At thirty-two killed Azog with his red axe before the East-gate of Moria; dissuaded Thráin II from entering Moria; Lord of the Iron Hills T.A. 2805-2941; came to the Battle of Five Armies with over five hundred Dwarves; became King under the Mountain after Thorin's fall and died aged 252 defending King Brand's body. (Dáin_II_Ironfoot redirects here.)

characters.name: Morgoth
clues: Mightiest of his kind, he wandered the Void seeking a flame that was not there.
His discords clashed with the Theme of the Creator, who answered with a second and a third Theme.
With the help of a spider he destroyed the Two Trees, killed Finwë at Formenos, and stole the Silmarils.
He was wounded seven times in single combat by a king of the Noldor, and one wound left him with a lasting limp.
Thrust into the Void after the War of Wrath, he is prophesied to return and be slain at the Last Battle by a hero of Men.

references.supports: Wandered the Void seeking the Flame Imperishable; his discords and Eru's second and third Themes; with Ungoliant destroyed the Two Trees, slew Finwë at Formenos and took the Silmarils; wounded seven times by Fingolfin, whose foot-wound left him a lasting limp; thrust into the Void after the War of Wrath; the Second Prophecy of Mandos.

characters.name: Maedhros
clues: Alone among his brothers, he refused to help burn the ships at Losgar, having hoped to send them back for a friend.
Captured through a feigned surrender of a jewel, he hung by one wrist from a steel shackle on a mountain for about thirty years.
Rescued by a friend with the help of the king of the Eagles, he lost his hand because the chain could not be broken.
He gave up the High Kingship to his uncle, and later formed a great union of Elves and Men that was broken at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad.
After the final war he stole one of the last two jewels with his brother, and burned by it, leapt into a fiery chasm.

references.supports: Alone of his brothers refused to help burn the ships at Losgar; captured by a feigned surrender, hung by a steel shackle on Thangorodrim for about thirty years; rescued by Fingon with Thorondor and lost his hand; gave up the High Kingship to Fingolfin; formed the Union of Maedhros, broken at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad; stole a Silmaril with Maglor and leapt into a chasm.
Maedhros had expected to send the ships back for Fingon; Fingon, carried by Thorondor, found Maedhros and cut off his hand because the chain could not be broken.

characters.name: Húrin
clues: He was shorter than the other men of his kin, taking after his mother's people, though in all else he resembled his strong, fiery-tempered grandfather.
His little daughter, whose name meant Laughter, died of a plague at the age of three.
At the Nirnaeth he held a rearguard with the men of his land, killing seventy foes and crying a battle-cry for each, until he was taken captive.
For refusing to reveal a hidden city, he was cursed and chained on a mountain, forced to watch his family's fate for twenty-eight years.
Freed at last, he slew a Dwarf who had betrayed his son, took a famed necklace, and threw it down before the king of Doriath.

references.supports: Shorter than other men of his kin, taking after his mother's people but otherwise like his grandfather Hador; his daughter Urwen (Lalaith, 'Laughter') died of plague aged three; held the rearguard at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad and cried a battle-cry for each of seventy foes slain before Gothmog bound him; cursed by Morgoth and chained on Thangorodrim for 28 years; killed Mîm, who had betrayed Túrin, took the Nauglamír and threw it before Thingol.

characters.name: Melian
clues: In the Gardens of Lórien, this Maia taught nightingales to sing.
After a dream warned her, she left her home across the Sea and led the Maiar who guarded the newly awakened Elves, the only woman among them.
Her blood passed to Elves and Men, for she is the only known Ainu to have had a child with one of the Children of Ilúvatar.
She alone repelled a monstrous spider from her kingdom, and her barrier kept out anyone less powerful than herself.
After her king's death she departed to mourn in the Halls of Mandos, and without her protection the realm fell.

references.supports: Taught nightingales to sing in the Gardens of Lórien; left Valinor after a warning in a dream and led the Maiar guarding the Elves at Cuiviénen, the only female among them; the only known Ainu to have had a child with a Child of Ilúvatar; alone repelled Ungoliant; the Girdle of Melian kept out anyone less powerful than her; after Thingol's death she left for the Halls of Mandos and Doriath fell.

characters.name: Beleg
clues: This Sinda, chief of the marchwardens of an Elven kingdom, was considered the best archer and huntsman of his time.
With a fellow captain, he was among the few Elves of his realm to fight at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad.
He sought out a fugitive friend, won a pardon from the king for him, and chose a sword the queen warned him was malicious.
He followed an orc-band into Taur-nu-Fuin, met an Elf of Nargothrond who had escaped slavery in the Dark Lord's mines, and rescued his friend during a thunderstorm.
While he cut his friend's bonds, his blade slipped; the friend awoke, seized the sword he had brought, and killed him by mistake.

references.supports: A Sinda, chief of the marchwardens and best archer and huntsman of his time; with Mablung one of the few Elves of Doriath at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad; won Thingol's pardon for Túrin and took Anglachel despite Melian's warning; followed Orcs into Taur-nu-Fuin, met Gwindor and rescued Túrin in a thunderstorm; slain by Túrin with Anglachel after the blade slipped while cutting his bonds.

characters.name: Glaurung
clues: Emerging while still young, this creature displeased his master, who allowed no further sallies for about two hundred years.
Fully grown, he led the greatest army yet of balrogs and orcs in the battle that broke a long siege.
At the Nirnaeth Arnoediad, he and his brood split two hosts apart; a Dwarf-lord whom he slew wounded his belly with a last stroke.
Though wingless, he breathed fire; with a spellbinding gaze he persuaded a hero to abandon a captive maiden, then lay on the hoard of a ruined Elven stronghold.
Ambushed in a gorge, he was dealt a mortal blow by a black sword; with his last breath he revealed his plot, and as he died his spell on a young woman was undone.

references.supports: Emerged still young in F.A. 260 and Morgoth allowed no sallies for about 200 years; fully grown at the Dagor Bragollach with the largest army of balrogs and orcs yet; at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad split the hosts of Maedhros and Fingon and was wounded in the belly by Azaghal; wingless fire-breather; spellbound Túrin into abandoning Finduilas and lay on the hoard of Nargothrond; ambushed at Cabed-en-Aras and killed by Gurthang; his last words revealed his plot and his spells were undone.

characters.name: Turgon
clues: When his wife fell into the waters on a crossing of ice, this prince saved only their daughter.
Guided by a dream from a Vala, he secretly led skilled craftsmen to build a hidden city in a vale, finishing it in the year 116.
Before leaving his first home, he left arms and armor there for one who would come in the Elves' hour of need.
He sent seven ships west to ask the Valar for help, but all were wrecked and only one sailor survived.
Warned to leave, he refused, ordered the gates of his realm blocked, and died defending his tower when the Dark Lord's host came.

references.supports: Saved only Idril when Elenwë fell into the waters on the Helcaraxe; guided by a dream from Ulmo, built Gondolin, finished F.A. 116; left a sword, mail and helm at Vinyamar for one who would come; with Círdan's help sent seven ships west, all wrecked, Voronwë the only survivor; refused Tuor's warning from Ulmo, blocked the Seven Gates and died defending the Tower of the King.

characters.name: Tuor
clues: A Man descended from all three Houses of the Edain, he was named by his father before he was born.
Fostered by Grey-elves, he was later a thrall of an Easterling chief for three years, then spent four years alone as an outlaw.
Guided by a sign from a Vala, he was the first Man to reach the Great Sea, then followed seven swans to an abandoned city and took the arms left there.
He carried a warning from a Vala to a hidden king, who refused it, and later wed that king's daughter.
When the hidden city fell, he threw a traitor from the walls and escaped with his wife by a secret way; their son's name meant Sea-friend.

references.supports: Descended from all Three Houses of the Edain, named by Huor before his birth; fostered by Annael's Elves; thrall of Lorgan for three years and then four years an outlaw; guided by Ulmo's sign, the first Man to reach the Great Sea, followed seven swans to the abandoned city of Vinyamar and took the arms left by Turgon; delivered Ulmo's warning to Turgon, who refused it, and married Idril; threw Maeglin from the walls and escaped with Idril; son Eärendil ('Sea-friend').
